name: Love bombing
looksLike: Intense closeness, praise, gifts, or 'you're my best friend' very early, before there's been time to earn it.
bodyCues: A rush, a flutter, a pull to match their intensity, and sometimes a small tightness underneath it.
selfQuestion: Is this pace matching how long we've actually known each other?
boundaryResponse: Enjoy it without accelerating. Keep the pace of sharing where the evidence is, not where the feeling is.

name: Guilt-tripping
looksLike: Making me responsible for their feelings to get what they want. 'After all I've done.' 'I guess I'm just not important to you.'
bodyCues: Heaviness in the chest, a sinking stomach, an urge to fix it right now.
selfQuestion: Whose feeling is this, and who is being asked to carry it?
boundaryResponse: 'I can hear you're disappointed. My answer is still no.' Their disappointment is theirs to carry.

name: Gaslighting
looksLike: Denying things that happened, rewriting conversations, or making me doubt my own memory. 'That never happened.' 'You're too sensitive.'
bodyCues: Fog, confusion, a spinning feeling, second-guessing what I clearly saw.
selfQuestion: What do I actually remember, before they told me what to remember?
boundaryResponse: 'We remember this differently, and I trust my memory.' Write down what happened while it's fresh.

name: DARVO
looksLike: When confronted: deny it, attack me for bringing it up, then reverse roles so they're the victim and I'm the offender.
bodyCues: Sudden defensiveness, then guilt, then confusion about who hurt whom.
selfQuestion: What was the original thing I raised, and did it get answered?
boundaryResponse: Return to the original point once. If it can't be discussed, that's the answer.

name: Moving goalposts
looksLike: Expectations keep shifting, so I never quite measure up. Every time I meet the bar, there's a new one.
bodyCues: Exhaustion, a treadmill feeling, trying harder with less to show for it.
selfQuestion: Have I ever actually been 'enough' for this person, at any point?
boundaryResponse: Stop chasing. 'I've done what I said I'd do. I'm not going to keep adding to it.'

name: Future faking
looksLike: Promises about the future that never materialize. Plans, trips, 'we should,' 'next time,' with no follow-through.
bodyCues: Hope that keeps getting re-lit, then a quiet drop each time.
selfQuestion: What has actually happened, versus what has been promised?
boundaryResponse: Trust the calendar, not the words. Hold plans loosely until they show up.

name: Boundary testing
looksLike: Small pushes after I've said no. 'Just this once.' 'Are you sure?' Asking again in a different way.
bodyCues: Tension, an urge to give in just to end it, resentment afterward.
selfQuestion: Did they accept my no the first time?
boundaryResponse: Repeat the no without new reasons. Reasons become things to argue with.

name: Triangulation
looksLike: Bringing others in to pressure or compare me. 'Everyone thinks…' 'So-and-so would do it.' Relaying what others supposedly said.
bodyCues: Feeling outnumbered, small, or suddenly on trial.
selfQuestion: Is this between me and them, or has a crowd been invited in?
boundaryResponse: 'I'm happy to talk with you about this directly.' Decline to respond to the crowd.

name: Intermittent reinforcement
looksLike: Hot and cold warmth that keeps me chasing. Wonderful one week, distant the next, with no clear reason.
bodyCues: Anxiety, checking my phone, relief that's too big when they finally respond.
selfQuestion: Am I working for warmth that a safe person would just give?
boundaryResponse: Match their consistency, not their peaks. Build from want, not need.

name: Isolation
looksLike: Discouraging my other relationships. Subtle criticism of my friends, jealousy of my time, 'they don't really get you like I do.'
bodyCues: A shrinking world, guilt about seeing other people.
selfQuestion: Has my circle gotten smaller since this person arrived?
boundaryResponse: Keep your people. 'My other friendships aren't up for discussion.'

name: Weaponized vulnerability
looksLike: Using what I shared in trust against me later, in an argument, as a joke, or to others.
bodyCues: A punched feeling, shame, an instinct to never share again with anyone.
selfQuestion: Was something I gave in trust used as a tool?
boundaryResponse: Share less, and say why. Graduated disclosure exists for exactly this.

name: Spiritual manipulation
looksLike: Using God, scripture, or 'the Lord told me' to control, shame, override my choices, or avoid accountability.
bodyCues: Confusion between guilt and conviction. Fear of disobeying God when I'm really being asked to obey a person.
selfQuestion: Does this line up with how Jesus actually treated people, or does it just use His name?
boundaryResponse: 'I'll take that to God myself.' God's voice doesn't need a middleman who benefits from the answer.

name: Chronic one-sidedness
looksLike: Taking consistently without giving. Only reaching out when they need something. Conversations that are all about them.
bodyCues: Depletion, a dread when their name comes up, resentment I feel guilty for.
selfQuestion: When did they last ask about me and wait for the answer?
boundaryResponse: Give from what you actually have. Let the Reciprocity Log tell the whole story.

name: Pity as leverage
looksLike: Using hardship to excuse repeated harm and avoid change. 'You know what I've been through.' The hardship is real, and it's also a shield.
bodyCues: Torn between compassion and something that knows this has happened too many times.
selfQuestion: Can I have compassion for their pain and still expect the behavior to change?
boundaryResponse: 'I'm sorry that's hard. I still need this to be different.' Both can be true.

name: Silent treatment as punishment
looksLike: Withdrawing, ignoring, or going cold to punish me until I give in or apologize for something I didn't do.
bodyCues: Panic, scrambling, an urge to over-apologize just to make it stop.
selfQuestion: Is this someone taking space, or someone making me pay?
boundaryResponse: Don't chase. 'I'm here when you're ready to talk.' Then go live your life.

name: Backhanded compliments and 'just joking' put-downs
looksLike: Digs disguised as humor or praise. 'You're so brave to wear that.' When I react: 'Relax, I'm just joking.'
bodyCues: A sting, then doubt about whether I'm allowed to feel the sting.
selfQuestion: If a kind friend heard that, would they laugh or wince?
boundaryResponse: 'That didn't feel like a joke to me.' You don't have to laugh to keep the peace.
